messages.subject: Re: [knitr] How to programatically tell the difference between a knitr and an Sweave Rnw file?
parts:
I do not think there is such a unique way of detection. It is
unavoidable that you have to scan for certain patterns such as
opts_chunk$set() or results='asis' for knitr, but it is not possible
to say for sure that one Rnw file is for Sweave only, because knitr
maintains compatibility with the Sweave syntax at the moment.

BTW, what is the context of this question?

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] How to programatically tell the difference between a knitr and an Sweave Rnw file?
parts:
On Wed, Dec 19, 2012 at 4:57 AM, Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I do not think there is such a unique way of detection. It is
> unavoidable that you have to scan for certain patterns such as
> opts_chunk$set() or results='asis' for knitr, but it is not possible
> to say for sure that one Rnw file is for Sweave only, because knitr
> maintains compatibility with the Sweave syntax at the moment.
>
> BTW, what is the context of this question?

A few. One example is automation. More importantly, long-term
reproducible research. As it stands, an *.Rnw file itself is not
enough to reproduce an analysis/report, but you also need to know
which of multiple commands to use for compiling the file, e.g. a
README file or a comment within the Rnw file. Compare with *.tex,
*.R, *.S, *.c, *.cpp etc - you pretty much know what to do with them
from their filename extensions.

Related, for now knitr is backward compatible with Sweave so you can
use knitr to process *.Rnw files (that's correct, eh?). But what
happens in the future when you choose to (or have to) break such
backward compatibility? A knitr-specific filename extension would
avoid this ambiguity. Just some thoughts.

Cheers,

Henrik

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] How to programatically tell the difference between a knitr and an Sweave Rnw file?
parts:
One way would be to take an approach similar to RStudio. It allows you to add the following lines to your Rnw document to control the weaving engine and the tex program.

% !Rnw weave = knitr
% !TeX program = XeLaTeX

Of course, this would tie people into RStudio, but from a reproducibility perspective, I think it works.

Just a thought.

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] How to programatically tell the difference between a knitr and an Sweave Rnw file?
parts:
I see your point, but I do not think there is a perfect solution. I do
not think there is anything perfectly "reproducible" in the world
without any instructions. It is trivial to invent a new filename
extension, but what is much much harder is to get major editors to
support it. Take R Markdown for example: in early versions of knitr, I
used the awkward filename foo_knit_.md instead of foo.Rmd just because
no editor knew the extension *.Rmd at that time. Now only RStudio
supports this file extension, which is enough at the moment.

I think I will break compatibility with Sweave one day for cleaner
maintenance, and users have to choose between Sweave and knitr.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] How to programatically tell the difference between a knitr and an Sweave Rnw file?
parts:
Just a quick follow-up:

1. As I said, knitr is no longer compatible with the Sweave syntax;
one has to make a choice between the two, although there is
Sweave2knitr() to help those who are not on the knitr boat yet:
http://yihui.name/knitr/demo/sweave/

2. R 3.0.0 will allow non-Sweave vignettes:
http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-devel/R-exts.html#Non_002dSweave-vignettes

The current method is to specify the weave engine in meta comments,
e.g. %\VignetteEngine{knitr}. In fact this also applies to R Markdown
vignettes (*.Rmd) which have also become first-class citizens in R
3.0.0. Brave beta testers can check out the latest development version
R from SVN and play with this brand new feature.

Regards,
